description: After an upload_document action, once its bytes are PUT to the upload URL: check them and add the document to its document set, which every ontology whose current version reads the set then reads (reads says how). Completing twice is no error.

use_case_run_id.description: An open run of a use case (helix_foundry_start_use_case_run) to record this upload under; empty for none.

workspace_id.description: Helix workspace identifier. May be empty when the caller has only one workspace (a service key always does).

name: helix_foundry_complete_document_upload

carried.description: Entities linked by a name a person linked to that entity in another document, which the load carries to every document.

names.description: What the load did with each decision on a name that met the document: its own resolve decisions, and the names carried from other documents where the load would otherwise have asked a person.

decision.description: resolve (the document's own decision on the name) or alias (a name a person linked to an entity in another document, carried to this one).

decision_id.description: The decision's id: of an alias, the resolve decision that linked the name.

outcome.description: written (applied in this load), not_asked (nothing in this load waited on it; it applies when the document is read again), not_named (the document doesn't name it) or refused (not applied; reason says why).

reason.description: Why it was refused: absent (the entity chosen isn't in the load), bound (the document's name is already linked another way; it changes when the document is read again), collides (another name in the document is already that entity), differs (the load no longer matches what the document gave; it applies when the document is read again), too_large (too large to write in place; the next load applies it), two_rows (another entity goes by the name too, or people linked it to different entities), role_term (a role, like the Customer, not a name), shared (another party in the document goes by it too), identifier (the document gives an identifier that doesn't match the entity), other_identity (the names show a different legal company), not_replayed (the document was read by an older version, or sent again without its reading; the next load applies it). Another reason means not applied in this load.

values.description: Values written: property values it stated that were written as evidence.

error_code.description: For failed: too_large (past a reading limit, such as a PDF of more than 150 pages or with more than 1 MiB of text) or unsupported (not what its type says, or a PDF that is damaged, encrypted, or scanned with no text layer).

error_message.description: For failed: why, and what to fix.

kind.description: How ontologies read the document: text (Markdown, MDX and plain text, extracted through routes as they are, and WebVTT transcripts, extracted as their turns, a line each), table (a CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL or Parquet file, read once at upload as a table of its own that mappings name by the document's id; it counts with synced tables toward the 50 tables a generation covers, and its cells are not extracted) or pdf (read once to its text, at upload or, for a Google Drive PDF, when its connection's sync writes it; loads extract that text through routes and generations read it as text).

retrying.description: A reading read waiting to run again after a failure that was not the file's.

rows.description: A table file's rows, once read.

state.description: ready (ontologies can read it: text, or a file whose read succeeded), reading (being read, or waiting to be: a generation started now leaves it out, and a load holding a PDF waits and reads it once the read ends) or failed (it can't be read: error_code and error_message say why, and a load records a failed PDF with the same code; upload a fixed file, or fix a connection's at its source).

at.description: The item's own time at the source, such as a note's creation; a connector's documents list newest first by it.

external_id.description: The key of its row at the source, such as a Granola note's id.

url.description: The item's page at the source.

version.description: The source's version of the row's text; new text at the source is a new document that replaces this one.

outcome.description: queued (an extract will read it), owed (the job running now reads it, or its end queues the extract that does), no_budget (the month's extraction budget is spent; the next load reads it), held (the current load already has it), skipped (the caller may not write that ontology's database) or reading (a PDF whose text is still being read: the load holds it and reads it once the read ends).

title: Complete a document upload
